About Alluvial Farms

Founded in 2015, Alluvial Farms is rooted in a passion for sustainable agriculture, animal welfare, and community connection. Located on the foothills of Sumas Mountain in Whatcom County, Washington, the farm produces pasture-raised, Animal Welfare Approved pork and value-added products for regional families who care about regenerative practices and knowing the farmers behind their food.

From the beginning, Alluvial has aimed to balance ecological health with productive agriculture—raising hogs outdoors on pasture, improving soil through rotational grazing, embracing whole-animal utilization, and enhancing ecosystem services. The result is pork that reflects both ethical care and exceptional quality, along with innovative offshoots like pet treats made from organ meats and handcrafted skin-care products made from rendered lard. Each product honors the animals and the land that sustain the farm.

Alluvial Farms is owned and operated by Matt McDermott, who brings more than twenty years of experience in sustainable agriculture, including a M.S. in Community and Agriculture, formal training in Ecological Horticulture, and collaboration with a variety of farm training and production systems.  Matt leads a small team of passionate land and animal stewards who share his vision of a regional food system built on transparency, integrity, and care. Together, they manage every step—from pasture to processing to customer—ensuring that each decision reflects respect for animals, people, and place.

Beyond production, Alluvial Farms opens its gates seasonally for on-farm events and tours, inviting the community to connect directly with the land, animals, and people behind their food.

Through this work, Alluvial Farms continues to pursue a simple but powerful mission: to raise animals humanely, manage land responsibly, and create nourishing products that strengthen both bodies and communities—one pasture at a time.

  
Thank you for your support!
Warmly,

MAY 29, 2025
Share

We are excited to announce that the Alluvial Farms Farmstand is now open!

6825 Goodwin Rd.  Everson, WA

We’ve been working to bring the model and partnerships to life and are thrilled to be open to the public every day from dawn to dusk. Stop on by for some sausages for grilling, sauerkraut to top them off, salad greens for tossing, farm fresh eggs for potato salad and so much more!

We teamed up with four local farms to make this farmstand come to life and allow customers a one stop shop experience for delicious local produce and meat.

Thank you to our partners!

Welcome to Alluvial Farms Farmstand where community and local food come together.

Featured Products include:

Produce - Spring Time Farm

Sauerkraut - Pangea Ferments

Fresh Eggs - Small Acres

Fireweed and Wildflower Honey - Bee Works

Pork Products - Alluvial Farms

Join Alluvial Pets Club

Let Alluvial Farms take care of hand making fresh pork liver dog treats for your family and delivering them to your mailbox each month for no additional cost.

We know your good intentions to feed your dog whole foods, and to upgrade their treats to whole foods with no fillers or chemical additives or stabilizers. 

And life is busy, we get it. 

At the end of a long day, reaching for the whole food pet treats to help encourage your dog to go for that last walk around the block before it’s dark leads to frustration when you realize all you have are the highly processed additive laden treats that had been easy to buy last time you were at the store. 

Situations like these are why we designed our Alluvial Pets Club. Enjoy a feeling of peace, calm and fulfillment at the end of your busy day when you can easily reach for a bag of Alluvial Farm pork liver pet treats each evening to take your dog for one final walk or training session.

We’ve offered your favorite pork/pet treats/salve and are now excited to introduce other complimentary products to our farm stand. For many years BeeWorks has kept hives at Alluvial through the spring season, and Pangea Ferments has dropped off their post-production vegetable scraps for the pigs year round. In 2025 Spring Time Farm started growing some of their organic vegetables on Alluvial ground as part of their crop rotation needs. These direct partnerships are important in a variety of ways and we’re thrilled to now be offering their high quality products, too.
